extraction.name: PASTIS
extraction.description: Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series (PASTIS), the first open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on SITS, with over 2 billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km2.
extraction.creator: Vivien Sainte Fare Gamot, Loic Landrieu
extraction.rai:dataCollection: PASTIS is comprised of 2 433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The time between acquisitions is uneven with a median of 5 days. This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each pixel of PASTIS is associated with a semantic label taken from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class. Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index. All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on SITS

name.evidence: We also introduce PASTIS, the first open-access SITS dataset with panoptic annotations.

description.evidence: Lastly, we present Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series (PASTIS), the first open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on SITS, with over 2 billion annotated pixels covering over 4000 km2.

url.evidence: This dataset, as well as more information about its composition, are publicly available at https://github.com/VSainteuf/pastis-benchmark .

datePublished.evidence: The values reported in this version of the article for the Panoptic Segmentation experiment differ from the version published in the ICCV 2021 proceedings.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: PASTIS is comprised of 2 433 sequences of multi-spectral images of shape 10×128×128. Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019 , for a total of over 2 billion pixels.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: The time between acquisitions is uneven with a median of 5 days. This lack of regularity is due to the automatic filtering of acquisitions with extensive cloud cover by the satellite data provider THEIA.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: Each sequence contains between 38 and 61 observations taken between September 2018 and November 2019

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The 10 channels correspond to the non-atmospheric spectral bands of the Sentinel-2 satellite, after atmospheric correction and re-sampling at a spatial resolution of 10 meters per pixel.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Each pixel of PASTIS is associated with a semantic label taken from a nomenclature of 18 crop types plus a background class... Each non-background pixel also has a unique instance label corresponding to its parcel index... All annotations are taken from the publicly available French Land Parcel Identification System.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: The French Payment Agency estimates the accuracy of the crop annotations via in situ control over 98% and the relative error in terms of surfaces under 0.3%.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Indeed, remote monitoring of the surface and nature of agricultural parcels is necessary for a fair allocation of agricultural subsidies ( 50 and 22 billion euros per year in Europe and in the US, respectively) and for ensuring that best crop rotation practices are respected.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: As is common in remote sensing applications, the dataset is highly unbalanced, with a ratio of over 50 between the most and least common classes.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We estimate that close to 28% of images have at least partial cloud cover.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Lastly, we present Panoptic Agricultural Satellite TIme-Series (PASTIS), the first open-access dataset for training and evaluating panoptic segmentation models on SITS
